content.text: {"abstained": false, "abstention_reason": "", "answer": "The NPS Vatsalya Scheme is a contributory saving and long-term financial security scheme designed exclusively for minors below 18 years of age [E01]. It was announced by the Finance Minister in the Union Budget for FY 2024-25 and is regulated by the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) [E01]. Parents or guardians can open accounts for their children with a minimum contribution of ₹250 per year with no maximum limit [E01]. The scheme offers multiple contribution modes including physical visits to registered service providers, online platforms, eNPS, and UPI apps [E02]. Guardians can partially withdraw up to 25% of contributions (excluding returns) after 3 years for education, medical treatment, or disability exceeding 75%, with up to 2 withdrawals allowed before age 18 and 2 additional withdrawals between ages 18-21 [E02][E03]. Upon reaching 18 years, subscribers can exit and withdraw up to 80% of accumulated corpus as a lump sum, with the balance used for annuity purchase; if the corpus is less than ₹8 Lakh, the entire amount can be withdrawn [E02][E03].
